Messages.Author: Yipe
Messages.Body:
Old player here returning to the game after 20 years and relearning some of the card interactions after being away for so long. I have a few questions about Form of Mist which seems like a fairly complex card:

1. Form of Mist vs Deflection
- Player A declares a bleed against Player B.
- Player B plays Deflection so the bleed is now targeting Player C.
- Player C successfully blocks Player A's vampire.
- Player A's and Player C's vampires enter combat.
- Player A plays superior Form of Mist and the combat ends.
- Player A's vampire burns 1 blood and continues the action at +1 stealth.

Is the target of the bleed still Player C, or does it revert back to the original target of the bleed action which is Player A?

2. When using the superior effect of Form of Mist to continue the action at +1 stealth, does all the previous stealth/intercept used for that action prior to combat still apply, or is it reset back to 0?

Messages.Author: Snodig
Messages.Body: It does precisely what it promises; it negates the block. All other properties of the action remain the same (as it’s still the same action).

Messages.Author: Yipe
Messages.Body:
Thank you for the replies!

In the case of the stealth/intercept still applying, I imagine if the blocking minion (who is now locked) can play a reaction card such as Wake With Evening's Freshness they can attempt to block again and they only need +1 intercept to match the acting vampire's stealth? Otherwise, a new unlocked minion must attempt to block the continuing action?

Messages.Author: Yomyael
Messages.Body:
> Yipe wrote:
> Thank you for the replies!
>
> In the case of the stealth/intercept still applying, I imagine if the blocking minion (who is now locked) can play a reaction card such as Wake With Evening's Freshness they can attempt to block again and they only need +1 intercept to match the acting vampire's stealth?
>
Yes. If the blocking minion was already locked and has played a wake (not an untap) to block, that still applies and you do not need to wake again.

> Yipe wrote:
> Otherwise, a new unlocked minion must attempt to block the continuing action?
>
If you do not have a wake, yes.

Prince of Bonn, Germany

Messages.Author: Yipe
Messages.Body:
Coming back to this topic briefly... we've picked up more players for our VtES group and we're getting in some regular games (or as much as possible considering the moratorium on in-person gaming and then wildfires hitting our area pretty hard right now).

Players are digging into some of their older cards/clans and building new decks to spice things up, which of course has led to further rules questions. The card in question this time around is Mirror Image, which functions in a similar capacity to Form of Mist (hence why I'm adding it to this discussion thread).

MIRROR IMAGE
[Chi] Action Modifier: +1 stealth
[CHI] Combat: Strike: combat ends. If this vampire was blocked while performing an action other than bleeding, the action continues as if unblocked.

The question is how to play Mirror Image at the superior level as it doesn't increase the acting minion's stealth like Form of Mist? If the blocking minion's previous intercept still applies, wouldn't combat end and then the action would be immediately blocked again and both minions would go right back into a new combat?

Is the purpose here to cycle your hand and hunt for more stealth? What are we missing? Our Ravnos player is looking for guidance to continue with their mind-altering shenanigans!

Messages.Author: Yipe
Messages.Body:
Huh, I guess I misunderstood how this works. When the initial blocking minion locks to block, and then the acting minion plays Mirror Image (or Form of Mist) to end combat, the blocking minion is no longer considered blocking?

But earlier in this thread, someone posted that if the blocking minion had played a wake (e.g. Wake with Evening's Freshness) to block the action, then they are still able to block this action because it hasn't been completed yet. That's a pretty complex and subtle distinction.

What if the initially blocking minion plays a wake card after the Mirror Image? Is all of the intercept they played to block in the first place still applicable here?

Messages.Author: Snodig
Messages.Body: Since it is still the same action, any modifiers and reactions (and others effects, like tap-for-stealth/int) still apply. This includes wakes already played by the blocker(s).

Messages.Author: Palamedes
Yipe
Messages.Body:
Gotcha. To clarify, if a minion blocked the initial declaration of the action then they would no longer be blocking the continued action unless:

A) They had previously played a wake card to block the action as it was started.
B) Play a wake card in response to the continuing action.

Whew, thanks!

You are correct, but remember, a minion blocked the initial declaration of the action does not tries to block the continued action automatically if he played wake before. You can make a new block attempt with that or any other minion.

Messages.Author: Yipe
Messages.Body:
> Palamedes wrote:
> You are correct, but remember, a minion blocked the initial declaration of the action does not tries to block the continued action automatically if he played wake before. You can make a new block attempt with that or any other minion.
>
Okay, based on what you just wrote I'm not sure I have this correct then.

Are you saying that the minion who initially blocked using a wake (and locked because the block was successful) can't automatically block the continued action? Is that because the minion is locked? But it's still the same action. This is really confusing. Here's an example:

1. Minion A takes the hunt action.
2. Minion B is locked and plays a wake.
3. Minion B plays enough intercept to successfully block and locks.
4. Minion A and B enter combat.
5. Minion A plays Form of Mist/Mirror Image as their strike. The action continues as if unblocked.

What can Minion B do now?

A) Minion B doesn't need to do anything new to block the continued action. They played a wake, this is the same action, and all intercept/stealth modifiers carry over. They simply declare they are blocking again even though they are locked and the 2 minions enter combat once more unless Minion A can gain more stealth.

B) Minion B must find a way to unlock or play another wake card to block the continued action. If they can, all intercept/stealth modifiers remain in place. Go to combat.

C) Minion B must find a way to unlock or play another wake card to block the continued action. No intercept/stealth modifiers carry over to this continued action.

D) None of the above? Something else? It's not really clear to me at all anymore.
